title: New Roads, Gas Stations, & Fire Dept Discipline
summary:
*   A fire department driver was suspended for reckless driving that damaged a fire truck and a building, injuring passengers; other firefighters were summoned for failing to intervene.
*   Permits were granted for installing new gasoline tanks and curbside pumps on Congress Avenue, and for a large oil storage facility, with specific safety and lighting regulations.
*   A major 11th Street paving project was approved, and a public hearing was scheduled for property owners to discuss how the costs would be assessed.
*   The city approved providing free water and light services for visiting U.S. Army and National Guard troops in September, and decided to sell condemned mules unfit for city work.

Paving 11th St
Notice to properly
owners, etc

Whereas, the City Council of the City of Austin, Texas, has heretofore determined to
improve 11th street from the east property line of Brazos street (North) to the east
prop-erty line of San Jacinto street, in the City of Austin, Texas, by paving the same
with Bitulithic pavement upon gravel concrete foundation with concrete gutters along curb
lines and necessary excavation, and has adopted specifications for said work and has
entered into a contract for the same with the Texas Bitulithic Company, a Corporation; and
Whereas, the City Engineer of the City of Austin, Texas, has this day filed his report in
writing with the City Council, showing the total cost of the said improvements upon the
said street, the amount per front foot of abutting property to be paid by the owners
therefrom, and also the names of persons, estates or Corporations owning property
abut-ting on said improvements, with a description of their property and a statement of
the total amount payable by each of said owners for said improvements; and Whereas, the
City Council has examined the said report and finds the same correct; and Whereas the
necessity exists that a portion of the cost of said improvements should be assessed
against said property owners and their property, subject to the terms of the Charter of
the City and the ordinance in such cases made and provided, and after the notice and
hearing provided by said Charter and ordinance; Now, therefore, Be it resolved by the City
Council of the City of Austin, Texas: 1. That the said report of the City Engineer be, and
the same is hereby approved and adopted.
2. That a portion of the cost of making the said improvements shall be assessed against
said owners of property abutting on 11 th street, in this City, from the east property
line

proportion as the frontage XX of each owner in each block of said street is to the whole
frontage in that block to be improved,provided that if such rule of apportionment shall
appear to the City Council to be unjust or unequal in any particular case ,or to result in

be made in excess of the actual benefits received by the owners of said property through
the enhanced value thereof by means of said improvement.

day of August ,A D 1916, at the Mayors office in the City Hall ,in the City of Austin,
Texas; at which hearing said property owners,their agents or attorneys shall be fully and

construct and maintain said
.tank or tanks as indicated; and
Whereas, the City Council is in all things satisfied with the site indicated herein and
upon a vote duly taken in all things approves the site so selected and the character of
storage tanks to be used: Be it therefore resolved by the City Council of the City of
Austin, acting herein by and through its Mayor and constitute' Councilmen: That the Dixie
Oil and Refining Company be and it is hereby granted permission to build and maintained on
the property above described one or more storage tanks for the reception and storage of
oil and oil products, gasoline and gasoline products, to be built on a rock ,brick or
concrete foundation, with all appurtenances or appliances requisite or incidental to the
right herein conferred.
The said Dixie Oil and Refining Company is hereby authorized and empowered to store or
warehouse in said tank or tanks oil and oil products ,gasoline and gasoline products in
excess of two hundred and fifty ( 250) gallons, standard measure.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none:
Approved, A F Wooldridge, Mayor.

Lawrence Hanley
Reckless Driving

The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: Whereas, in the judgement of
the City Council ,Lawrence Hanley , the then driver of North Austin Hose Company No 5,was
guilty of reckless driving in driving the car of said North Austin Hose Co No 5 to a
reported fire at 1505 Colorado street on the night of Friday August 18th 1916, in that by
reason of said reckless driving the greatly injured the car he was driving and destroyed
the store building situated at the corner of 19th and


 --- Page break --- 

590

Guadalupe streets in this City, and more or less injured all of the persons upon said car
which the said Lawrence Hanley was driving.

Now, therefore,
Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin, Texas : That in punishment for
said reckless driving which in the judgement of the City Council constitutes a breach of
the necessary discipline to be enforced in said Austin Fire Department, the said Lawrence
Hanley is hereby suspended from occupation and pay from the 20th day of August 1916, to
the 1st day of January 1917, and Be it further resolved by the City Council of the City of
Austin, Texas: That James Quinlan and John Luckey be and they are hereby summonsed to
appear before the City Council at its meeting to be held on Thursday, the 24th day of
August, 2916, to receive a public reprimand for failure to remonstrate with the said
Lawrence Hanley for the reckless gate at which he was driving said North Austin Hose Co No
5 car.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none:
Approved , A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
